title: Study permit: Who can apply
text: To come to Canada to study, an applicant must be enrolled at a designated learning institution (DLI). The applicant must also show enough money to pay tuition, living expenses for themselves and any accompanying family members, and return transportation for everyone. The applicant must obey the law, have no criminal record and obtain a police certificate if one is required. The applicant must be in good health and complete a medical exam if required. Finally, the applicant must convince an officer that they will leave Canada when the study permit expires.

title: Study permit: Provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter
text: A provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter (PAL/TAL) comes from the province or territory where the student plans to study and confirms that a place is available. It is provided through the designated learning institution and is usually required to apply for a study permit. It must be submitted together with the study permit application, not afterwards, and for each applicant even when a family applies together.

title: Study permit: Provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter
text: No PAL or TAL is needed for several groups, including students applying to preschool, primary or secondary school, and students entering a degree-granting master's or doctoral program at a public DLI starting January 1, 2026. Exchange students who pay no tuition to the Canadian institution, and holders of a Global Affairs Canada scholarship, are also exempt. An applicant who claims an exemption must provide proof of it with the application.

title: Study permit: Provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter
section: How long a PAL/TAL is valid
text: A PAL/TAL is linked to the school the student applies to and normally has to be used in the year it was issued. For the 2026 cap year, a PAL/TAL issued between January 1, 2026 and December 31, 2026 is valid until December 31, 2026. A letter from a previous cap year cannot be used, and an expired letter must be replaced by a new one before applying. A new letter is also needed after a refusal or approval, or when changing schools.

title: Study permit: Provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter
text: Students who want to study in Quebec need an attestation of issuance of a Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ) from the Government of Quebec instead of a PAL. Most students who are exempt from the PAL must still obtain a CAQ. The CAQ must contain the line stating that the applicant has a place in Quebec's share of study permit applications or is exempt from it.

title: Study permit: Proof of financial support
text: Applicants must prove they have enough money, without working in Canada, to cover tuition, living expenses for themselves and accompanying family members, and transportation to and from Canada. Funds for the first year of studies must be shown. For programs longer than one year, the applicant must also explain how the whole program will be paid, for example with a multi-year scholarship or employed parents.

title: Study permit: Proof of financial support
text: Examples of documents that can show funds include a receipt for the first year of tuition and housing, a student loan from a bank, a scholarship, pay stubs, a signed letter from a sponsor with proof of their occupation and relationship, a Canadian bank account in the applicant's name, a guaranteed investment certificate from a Canadian financial institution, and bank statements for the past six months. The list is not complete and applicants need not provide all of these documents. Bank statements must show where the income comes from.

title: Study permit: Proof of financial support
text: For applications submitted on or after September 1, 2026, outside Quebec, the living expense amount for one person is 23,448 Canadian dollars per year, 29,192 for two people, 35,888 for three, and 43,572 for four. These amounts exclude tuition and transportation costs. For applications between January 1, 2025 and August 31, 2026, the amount for one person was 22,895 dollars. Quebec applicants must follow the costs set by the Quebec immigration ministry.

title: Study permit: How to apply
text: When applying, the applicant should submit the letter of acceptance from the designated learning institution, the provincial or territorial attestation letter, and as many of the other required documents as possible. A study permit cannot be finalized until the application is complete, and waiting to submit documents delays processing. Applications for a study permit must be made online, with limited exceptions such as a disability that prevents online application.

title: Study permit: How to apply
text: Most applicants between 14 and 79 years old must give fingerprints and a photo, called biometrics. The biometrics fee of 85 Canadian dollars for an individual, or at most 170 for families applying together, should be paid when the application is submitted. The applicant has 30 days from the date of the letter to give biometrics, and they are only needed once every 10 years.
